findings: H1/Q2 2026 earnings cluster (~12 May): yfinance summaries state Imperial remained on track for full-year targets after H1 tobacco and NGP net revenue growth; management flagged one-off headwinds in the U.S. and Australia and progress on Evolve 2030 (articles e3aaefb7, 4a824cd0; source: docs/data/research_director_worker/IMB.L/20260904T174213Z/sources/news_manifest.json).
Q2 2026 earnings-call RSS/yfinance note (~12 May): steady financial performance with revenue growth and strategic initiatives, alongside market-share and NGP challenges (article 4a824cd0).
Morningstar post-earnings RSS title (~13 May): shares look undervalued and second half of the year should improve; no statutory H1 figures in manifest (article 1c0fa8aa).

Black Buffalo nicotine-pouch acquisition (~27 May): Imperial to spend at least $150m (£111.6m) on U.S. pouch maker Black Buffalo; shares reversed earlier losses on the announcement (article 4a1187d5).

Strategy 2030 / FY2026 start (~2 Jun): executives cited a strong start to the 2026 financial year under Strategy 2030, emphasising disciplined NGP growth, combustibles value creation and a multiyear efficiency programme (article 234f68e1).
Job cuts and savings (~10 Aug): Imperial cutting thousands of jobs in the U.S. and Europe; group employs about 25,800 people globally; plan targets £320m annual savings by 2030 (article f9f7a120).

April 2026 sell-off cluster (~14 Apr): multiple RSS titles report shares down ~7% while fiscal 2026 outlook was reaffirmed; drivers cited include Middle East conflict uncertainty and sector pricing dynamics (articles dd33dec9, 30c7acb0, 8242b96b, 6a51c1eb, 9b688d33).
UK youth cigarette ban (~28 Apr): RSS title notes stock dip on the ban but outlook remains positive (article 16e1433c).
Deutsche Bank (~15 Apr): sell-off characterised as overreaction (articles 07b0f378, a60d3dc1).
Bank of America upgrade (~15 Jul): RSS title cites improving outlook and attractive valuation; no target price or rating change detail in manifest (article 39ddadfb).
Morningstar valuation concern (~15 Apr): RSS title places shares near undervalued range but flags combustibles and nicotine-pouch concerns (article 68a909a6).
Simply Wall St ex-dividend cluster: income investors alerted ahead of ex-dividend (articles 0c2dbb391 ~16 Aug, 83f1e512 ~8 Jul); separate RSS item references a UK£0.4008 dividend (article 8ee903774).

£1.45bn share buyback programme (collapsed from ~20 Kalkine/TipRanks/Globe daily tranche reprints, Aug–Jul 2026): ongoing disclosed capital-management programme with routine repurchases/cancellations; sample August tranche prices cited at 2,497p–2,767p; July 2026 cancellation of 218,190 shares noted (articles d98704eb, 7970488d, c5270cb4, f854eb8d, f7d8f8e5, 1e2bd09c, f5e39200; others discarded as duplicate programme prints).
Analyst caution (~29 May): fair value estimate trimmed from £34.65 to £33.14 amid growing caution (article f19ab314).

Discarded as non-IMB.L or filler per brief: ASX:IMB / Intelligent Monitoring Group / ADT UK (articles c33abf47, 1d2059b5, 22513698); BAT+IMB cannabis pairing pieces (articles abb48065, be66db2b, 4a8f6d13, 1a3b1d82, 48cda994, 7b046fc8); UK income/ETF listicles and duplicate Kalkine income reprints (articles 7c6cbff6, 5a66a7d8, 73767fcc, e124d231, 56774867, 7be4e003, 99ce836e, 3c10e755, etc.).
